sources.title: Sperm DNA fragmentation: how to test, when to test, and what to do with abnormal results. A pragmatic mini-review for clinical practice
sources.claim: Assays TUNEL, SCSA, SCD, Comet are not interchangeable; assay-specific thresholds (SCSA 25% diagnosis, 30-35% IVF/ICSI; TUNEL 17% diagnosis; SCD 16-20%); many centers treat 20% or more as actionable and 30% or more as high; tier 1 indications: unexplained infertility, RPL, failed IUI after 2-3 cycles, prior ART failure, clinical varicocele; tier 2: infection, obesity, diabetes, smoking, advanced paternal age, toxin exposure; optimization (lifestyle, weight loss, infection treatment, varicocele repair) associated with about 20-40% SDF reduction; antioxidants should not be prescribed reflexively; testicular sperm ICSI considered when SDF stays above 30% despite optimization, mainly after ART failure, evidence low-certainty; abstinence about 2-3 days; repeat test after about 10-12 weeks
sources.quote: These values serve as decision-support tools, not absolute cut-offs; antioxidant therapy should not be prescribed reflexively in response to an abnormal SDF result; repeating SDF testing approximately one spermatogenic cycle (~10-12 weeks) after the initial test; Testi-ICSI is therefore not proposed as a substitute for andrological optimization

sources.title: The effect of sperm DNA fragmentation on miscarriage rates: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.claim: 16 cohort studies, 2,969 couples; miscarriage risk higher with high sperm DNA damage, RR 2.16
sources.quote: Miscarriage rates are positively correlated with sperm DNA damage levels; RR = 2.16 (CI 1.54-3.03), P < 0.00001; 16 cohort studies (2969 couples)

sources.title: Sperm DNA fragmentation and assisted reproduction: an umbrella meta-analysis
sources.claim: 8 meta-analyses, more than 25,000 ART cycles; high SDF linked to lower clinical pregnancy in IVF (RR 0.66) and IUI (RR 0.47), higher miscarriage after ICSI (RR 2.29), lower live birth in IVF (RR 0.79), ICSI live birth not significantly different (RR 0.94); certainty low; testing best used as an adjunct, not a routine stand-alone test
sources.quote: Miscarriage ICSI 2.286 (1.383-3.779); clinical pregnancy IVF 0.662 (0.547-0.801); IUI 0.467 (0.242-0.900); live birth IVF 0.792 (0.638-0.983); ICSI 0.941 (0.721-1.228); GRADE certainty low for all outcomes

sources.title: Diagnosis and treatment of infertility in men: AUA/ASRM guideline part I
sources.claim: SDF testing not recommended in the initial evaluation of the infertile couple; for couples with RPL, men should be evaluated with karyotype and sperm DNA fragmentation; at least two semen analyses ideally a month apart
sources.quote: Sperm DNA fragmentation analysis is not recommended in the initial evaluation of the infertile couple; For couples with RPL, men should be evaluated with karyotype (Expert Opinion) and sperm DNA fragmentation

sources.title: ESHRE guideline: recurrent pregnancy loss: an update in 2022
sources.claim: Assessing sperm DNA fragmentation in couples with RPL could be considered; RPL defined as loss of two or more pregnancies
sources.quote: Assessing sperm DNA fragmentation in couples with RPL could be considered for diagnostic purposes; RPL is defined as the loss of two or more pregnancies

sources.title: The effects of varicocelectomy on the DNA fragmentation index and other sperm parameters: a meta-analysis
sources.claim: 7 prospective studies, 289 patients; DNA fragmentation index fell by 6.86 percentage points after varicocelectomy
sources.quote: After varicocelectomy, the sperm DFI decreased by 6.86%

sources.title: Superior Live Birth Rates, Reducing Sperm DNA Fragmentation (SDF), and Lowering Miscarriage Rates by Using Testicular Sperm Versus Ejaculates in ICSI Cycles from Couples with High SDF: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.claim: 13 studies; 530 men in SDF analysis; testicular sperm SDF about 25 points lower; live birth OR 2.40; miscarriage OR 0.31; moderate to serious risk of bias
sources.quote: Paired assessments of SDF showed significantly lower levels in testicular sperm compared to ejaculated sperm; live birth OR 2.40 (1.32-4.36); miscarriage OR 0.31 (0.14-0.70); the studies included were rated as having a moderate to serious risk of bias
